oneirgeo.drawing.use: A house, three people and a sun going down. The smallest person is coloured in black.
oneirgeo.dream.faded: The dream lets go of you
oneirgeo.fragment.0: the house had a red carpet. I remember the carpet.
oneirgeo.fragment.1: we used to watch the telephone lines at dusk
oneirgeo.fragment.10: the doctor said it was only a fever
oneirgeo.fragment.11: there is a door in every dream. it is always the same door.
oneirgeo.fragment.12: the sea was so still I could see myself walking upside down
oneirgeo.fragment.13: we buried something under the observatory. I forget what.
oneirgeo.fragment.14: the hum never stops. you stop hearing it.
oneirgeo.fragment.16: I tried to wake up and woke up here
oneirgeo.fragment.17: all the clocks in the house stopped at the same minute
oneirgeo.fragment.18: it follows the way you came, not the way you go
oneirgeo.fragment.19: the tissue remembers being a thought
oneirgeo.fragment.2: someone was calling my name from the next room
oneirgeo.fragment.20: don't look at the tall one for too long. don't look away either.
oneirgeo.fragment.21: the barrels in the dark rooms are not all barrels
oneirgeo.fragment.22: I wrote this so I would remember. I don't.
oneirgeo.fragment.23: there is someone standing where the fog thins
oneirgeo.fragment.3: the pool closed in September. nobody told the water.
oneirgeo.fragment.4: I counted the doors twice. there were more the second time.
oneirgeo.fragment.5: the stars were wrong that night too
oneirgeo.fragment.6: my hands were smaller when I last stood here
oneirgeo.fragment.7: if you are reading this, you fell asleep again
oneirgeo.fragment.9: I left the light on so you could find the way back
oneirgeo.iv.use: The bag is almost empty. Someone keeps refilling it.
oneirgeo.journal.found: There is a notebook in your pocket. A few of its pages are in your handwriting.
oneirgeo.journal.intro: Things I remembered, in the order they came back.
oneirgeo.journal.last.0: It is still 3:17. It has been 3:17 for %s years.
oneirgeo.journal.last.1: Every whisper was them. Every "wake up" was them. The light is still on.
oneirgeo.journal.last.2: The stairs under the house go further down now.
oneirgeo.journal.title: Dream Journal
oneirgeo.lifeguard.rescue: A whistle. Someone pulls you out of the deep end.
oneirgeo.marble.use: It is cold, and there is a tiny house inside it.
oneirgeo.mirror.blocked: Something is standing in the way on the other side of the glass.
oneirgeo.mirror.dive: You sink through your own reflection.
oneirgeo.mirror.surface: You come up through the glass. Nobody is waiting on the other side.
oneirgeo.monitor.use: The line on the screen climbs, falls, and climbs again.
oneirgeo.nurse.bed: Someone takes your hand and leads you back to bed.
oneirgeo.phone.1: the doctor says you can hear us. so I'll keep talking.
oneirgeo.phone.2: we brought your star map. it's on the table by the window.
oneirgeo.phone.3: it's raining here. you always liked the rain.
oneirgeo.phone.4: your room is just the way you left it.
oneirgeo.phone.6: [a dial tone, then your own voice, much younger: "coming!"]
oneirgeo.phone.7: dad says he'll bring the camcorder tomorrow.
oneirgeo.phone.8: it's 3:17 again. it's always 3:17 when I call.
oneirgeo.phone.tone: A dial tone. It sounds a long way off.
oneirgeo.story.all: You remember everything. The stairs under the house go further down now.
oneirgeo.story.complete: You remember %s. There is a tape in your pocket.
oneirgeo.story.fever.0: The fever came the next morning. Everything was too bright and too far away.
oneirgeo.story.fever.1: Forty-one point two. I heard the number and saw it burning.
oneirgeo.story.fever.2: The doctor said it was only a fever. He said it twice. The second time he said it to mom.
oneirgeo.story.fever.3: They put me in a bath of ice. I dreamed of furnaces that had gone out, and I was the last warm thing in them.
oneirgeo.story.fever.4: The ceiling was upside down, or I was. A whole city hung from it and nobody fell.
oneirgeo.story.fever.5: Mom's hand was cool on my face. Then it was gone, and the room was very loud.
oneirgeo.story.fever.6: Somebody said "seizure". At 3:17 every clock in the house stopped, even the ones that were far away.
oneirgeo.story.final: The room where the clocks stopped. The light is still on.
oneirgeo.story.house.0: The house had a red carpet on the stairs. I counted the steps every night: fourteen. There are more now.
oneirgeo.story.house.1: At dusk the telephone lines hummed. Dad said it was people talking far away. I think it was the wires remembering.
oneirgeo.story.house.2: Mom called me from the kitchen. I said "coming". I am still on my way.
oneirgeo.story.house.3: My room was at the end of the hall. The door stuck in summer; I learned to open it with my shoulder.
oneirgeo.story.house.4: There was a crack in my ceiling shaped like a river. I followed it with my eyes every night until I fell asleep. Here every crack is a river.
oneirgeo.story.house.5: Dad filmed everything with his camcorder. "For later," he said. I didn't know later meant this.
oneirgeo.story.house.6: The last night in the house I had a headache. Mom put a cold towel on my forehead and turned off the light. I asked her to leave it on.
oneirgeo.story.observatory.0: Before the fever, dad took me to the observatory on the hill. It was the best night of the summer.
oneirgeo.story.observatory.1: He showed me how to find the pole star. "If you're ever lost, it stays where it is."
oneirgeo.story.observatory.2: We counted the moons of Jupiter. I counted one more than there were. He didn't correct me.
oneirgeo.story.observatory.3: We buried a tin box under the observatory floor, right below the telescope: a drawing, a tape and a marble. "Open it when you're grown up."
oneirgeo.story.observatory.4: Dad wrote the numbers on the back of the star map so we could find it again: %s, %s.
oneirgeo.story.observatory.5: Now the stars are wrong. There is an eye where the moon should be. I think it is looking for me too.
oneirgeo.story.observatory.6: Every night the sky turns back a little. Maybe it is trying to get back to that night.
oneirgeo.story.pool.0: On the last day of summer we went to the public pool. The water was as warm as a bath.
oneirgeo.story.pool.1: I held my breath and stayed at the bottom as long as I could. The lifeguard blew his whistle.
oneirgeo.story.pool.2: Water went up my nose. It burned. I laughed and did it again.
oneirgeo.story.pool.3: That night my head hurt behind my eyes, as if the water was still in there.
oneirgeo.story.pool.4: The pool closed in September. Nobody told the water. It is still waiting for us to come back.
oneirgeo.story.pool.5: Someone asked mom whether I had been swimming. She cried for a long time after that.
oneirgeo.story.pool.6: Every pool here is that pool. Every lifeguard is that lifeguard. He is still watching the deep end.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.0: The sea is so still it shows me upside down. My reflection is taller than me.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.1: My reflection's hands are bigger than mine. It has a scar I don't have yet.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.2: It moves a moment after I do. Or I move a moment after it.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.3: Mirrors don't show the room. They show the room as it will be when nobody is in it.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.4: I asked my reflection how old I am. It counted on its fingers and ran out of fingers.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.5: Under the surface there is another world, the same as this one, where I am awake.
oneirgeo.story.reflection.6: If I go down there, it comes up here. We can't both be awake.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.0: The hospital corridor had lights that hummed like the telephone lines. Mom and dad sat under them for a long time.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.1: The vending machine had my favourite drink. Dad bought one every day and never drank it.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.2: The nurse said I could hear them. So they talked: about the house, the stars, the pool.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.3: Days stopped having names. The yellow walls stayed the same colour for years.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.4: They asked mom whether to keep the light on. She said yes. She says yes every time.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.5: Dad reads to me now. His voice comes through the walls, slower than it should be.
oneirgeo.story.waiting.6: There is a door at the end of every corridor. It is always the same door. On the other side, someone is holding my hand.
oneirgeo.supply.arrived: There is something in your pocket that was not there before
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.0: [dad's face, too close to the lens]
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.1: DAD: hi. if you're watching this, you're grown up now.
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.2: DAD: I hope it was a good life. I hope we were there for all of it.
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.3: DAD: if you ever get lost, count the stairs at home. there were always fourteen.
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.4: [he looks away from the camera for a long time]
oneirgeo.tape.capsule.label: OPEN WHEN YOU'RE GROWN UP
oneirgeo.tape.fever.0: [no picture. the lens cap is still on]
oneirgeo.tape.fever.1: MOM: forty-one point two. call him again.
oneirgeo.tape.fever.2: DAD: the line's busy. it's been busy for an hour.
oneirgeo.tape.fever.3: [a cold cloth being wrung out. water dripping into a bowl]
oneirgeo.tape.fever.4: YOU: is the house on fire? it's so hot in here
oneirgeo.tape.fever.label: (no label)
oneirgeo.tape.final.0: [a hospital room. a bed. a machine counts something, slowly]
oneirgeo.tape.final.1: [on the wall, a clock that says 3:17. it has said 3:17 for a long time]
oneirgeo.tape.final.2: [the camcorder is on a tripod by the window. its red light is on]
oneirgeo.tape.final.4: DAD: whenever you're ready. there's no hurry.
oneirgeo.tape.glitch.0: [you, asleep, in a room you don't remember]
oneirgeo.tape.glitch.1: [someone off camera: is it still recording?]
oneirgeo.tape.house.0: [a hallway. a red carpet runs up the stairs]
oneirgeo.tape.house.2: [you wave. you are missing a front tooth]
oneirgeo.tape.house.3: MOM (from the kitchen): dinner's ready - come down, both of you
oneirgeo.tape.house.4: [the camera turns to the window. the sun is setting. it keeps setting]
oneirgeo.tape.house.label: HOME - DON'T TAPE OVER
oneirgeo.tape.no_player: There is nothing here to play it on.
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.0: [the dome of the observatory opens. stars, too many to count]
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.1: DAD: that one's the pole star. it stays where it is.
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.2: YOU: what if I get lost somewhere it can't see?
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.3: DAD: then I'll come and find you. I'll bring the camera.
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.4: [you both laugh. the tape runs out]
oneirgeo.tape.observatory.label: STARS W/ KIDDO
oneirgeo.tape.pool.0: [a public pool, blue and loud. a whistle somewhere]
oneirgeo.tape.pool.1: DAD: one more dive and then we're going home
oneirgeo.tape.pool.2: [you jump. the camera follows the splash, and waits]
oneirgeo.tape.pool.3: [you come up laughing. you rub your forehead]
oneirgeo.tape.pool.4: LIFEGUARD: the pool's closing for the season, folks
oneirgeo.tape.pool.label: LAST SWIM OF SUMMER
oneirgeo.tape.reflection.0: [a mirror. you in it, older than you are]
oneirgeo.tape.reflection.1: [the reflection lifts its hand a moment after you do]
oneirgeo.tape.reflection.2: [it mouths something. it might be your name. it might be its own]
oneirgeo.tape.reflection.3: [it turns around and walks deeper into the glass]
oneirgeo.tape.reflection.label: (blank)
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.0: [a corridor. yellow walls. fluorescent lights humming]
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.1: [mom asleep in a plastic chair, holding a cold cup of tea]
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.2: DAD (quietly): the nurse says you can hear us.
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.3: DAD: so we'll keep talking. we'll keep the light on.
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.4: [the date in the corner keeps changing. the corridor doesn't]
oneirgeo.tape.waiting.label: HOSPITAL
oneirgeo.telescope.here: The brightest star is right overhead. Whatever it marks is under your feet.
oneirgeo.telescope.nothing: Only fog, and the shapes of things too far away to name.
oneirgeo.telescope.star: One star burns brighter than the rest, low over the %s, about %s blocks away.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.0: Only snow. For a moment it looks like a hallway.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.1: Snow, and very faintly, a laugh track.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.2: The snow spells nothing. You read it anyway: STAY.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.3: A test card, then a date: SEP. 14 1997.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.4: Snow. Behind it, someone is filming this television.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.5: A weather report for a town you used to know. Fog, all week.
oneirgeo.tv.snow.7: Snow. It is warm, like breath on glass.
oneirgeo.whisper.14: the floor is very far down
oneirgeo.whisper.18: you dropped something a long time ago
oneirgeo.whisper.2: it is later than you think
oneirgeo.whisper.21: the sun has been setting for years
oneirgeo.whisper.6: remember the colour of the sky
oneirgeo.whisper.9: it was smaller when you were small
